adjudication_rationale: I side with coder B: Balance is a DLRM CPU thread/runtime scheduler for core allocation, work stealing, and table reordering, which is orchestration above a concrete kernel implementation.
I side with coder A: POD-Attention is explicitly a new GPU attention kernel for hybrid prefill/decode batches, with fusion and SM-aware CTA scheduling as secondary mechanisms.

I side with coder A: LeanAttention is an optimized exact attention execution mechanism/kernel for transformer decode, while its Stream-K-style work partitioning is the scheduling mechanism behind the kernel.

I side with coder A: HyC-LoRA makes activation quantization/compression a primary mechanism and implements custom Triton backward/fused operators, so it is precision-format work with kernel support rather than compression only.

I side with coder A: TileLink is a compiler/DSL framework that lowers tile-centric primitives into overlapped compute-communication GPU kernels; fusion and scheduling are secondary aspects of the generated kernels.

I side with coder B: TASDER/TASD maps unstructured sparse DNN tensors into structured sparse tensor sequences usable by existing structured sparse accelerators, including a real RTX 3080 demonstration.
